entities.summary: Lê Tương Dực, birth name Lê Oanh (黎瀠), reigned from 1509 to 1516, was the ninth emperor of the later Lê dynasty of Đại Việt. The only primary account of his life and reign was the Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư, the official historical chronicle of Đại Việt during the Lê dynasty which was completed in 1697 under the direction of the Trịnh lords. The chronicle described Lê Tương Dực as initially being a good emperor who reorganized the court and ruled the nation wisely. However, later during his reign, he became overly greedy, corrupt and extravagant.

entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lê Tương Dực, born Lê Oanh (黎瀠), was the ninth emperor of the Later Lê dynasty of Đại Việt (Vietnam), reigning from 1509 to 1516. His reign is recorded primarily in the Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư, the comprehensive official history of Vietnam. He came to power through a coup that deposed the previous emperor Lê Uy Mục, whose own brutal reign had sparked aristocratic revolt.

Lê Tương Dực's reign began as a restoration of order after Uy Mục's excesses, but rapidly acquired its own reputation for tyranny and extravagance. Court sources record that he devoted enormous resources to construction projects in Thăng Long (Hanoi), including a vast palace complex, while neglecting military affairs and administration. He is described as prone to dissolute pleasures and indifferent to governance — the standard characterization of a 'bad last emperor' in Confucian historiography.

His reign ended in 1516 when the general Trần Cảo, originally a rebel leader, seized the capital. Lê Tương Dực was killed during the revolt. His fall inaugurated a prolonged period of internal conflict in Đại Việt, as the Later Lê dynasty was reduced to a puppet monarchy while actual power was contested among powerful regional lords — a situation that would persist until the Mac dynasty seized nominal power in 1527 and the country entered decades of civil war between the Mac and restored Lê supporters.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Lê Tương Dực's reign marked a brief period of relative stability in Đại Việt after Lê Uy Mục's brutal rule, but his own extravagance and neglect of governance led to instability and paved the way for future aristocratic revolts.
